mentl/0fa3649:
expect_same was the lone unify arm that bound a var without chasing, so a scalar
clobbered a constructor argument's NBound(TVar(binder)) live binding and the
parameter never learned its declared field type. A Float positional ctor field
from an unannotated param (type Box = MkBox(Float); fn wrap(g) = MkBox(g)) left g
an unresolved var, floored to i32, and the f64 call site trapped indirect-call —
the ctor-arg face of the float-evidence-ft class, which also blocked LSP serve on
json's parse_number Float.

The one-line fix chases the var live, like every other unify arm. It unmasked the
runtime's pervasive handle-word pun (a handle IS a word, so String/List handles
were used as raw Int addresses), which foundational correctness closes by typing
the string layer whole: byte_len/byte_at/str_slice/str_concat/view_base and the
float builders are seq-ops over self-consistent raw bodies (the list_index
pattern); str_of_buf is the one construction boundary (a raw [len][bytes] buffer
word IS a String), coerced at every builder return; the parse and comment
functions read via byte_at/byte_len, not raw arithmetic; state slots dedup by
handle identity (i32.eq) via handle_recorded, never str_eq.

Two convergent shortcuts were built and refuted by the binary first: typing
byte_len as String spread the census (the string layer is uniformly raw-Int),
and address-permissive memory ops is blocked because s + 12 forces Int through +.
The census drove 10 -> 17 -> 15 -> 8 -> 2 -> 0 across six m2 builds.

Full-wheel census 0; the LSP json float blocker cleared (serve reaches the LSP
layer; hover-response is the next rung). TRANSITION m3 == m4, boot re-pinned from

mentl/0fe2839:
Wraps gradient_next's internal Option<(Annotation, Capability)>
result into the public AnnotationSuggestion(SuggestionKind, String,
List, Reason) shape at the boundary. Adds five helpers:
to_annotation_suggestion (the wrap), suggestion_kind_of (Annotation
→ SuggestionKind tag-only mapping; drift 8 closure — never a
string flag), capability_labels (List<Capability> → List<String>
for transport rendering), suggestion_reason (Located/Inferred wrap
threading the candidate's anchor reason into the Why chain),

variant for the Located span), suggestion_kind_label (label per
SuggestionKind for the inner Inferred reason).

The body of gradient_next is otherwise unchanged: same enumeration
(base candidates + ownership candidates), same speculative oracle
(checkpoint → apply → verify → rollback per try_each_annotation),
same pick_highest_leverage. The boundary wrap turns the lossy
single-Capability return into the multi-capability list per
capabilities_for_annotation, surfacing the actual gradient unlocks
not the artificially-reduced first one.

mentl/0f0f26b:
'pipe_tee' was a generic tag — every ~> handler installation
looked identical in the handler_stack. When hover or diagnostics
read the stack, they saw 'pipe_tee' instead of 'env_handler',
'graph_handler', 'diagnostics_handler'.

Now uses callee_name(right) to extract the authored handler name
from the RHS node. The handler_stack carries:
  ['diagnostics_handler', 'graph_handler', 'env_handler', ...]
instead of:
  ['pipe_tee', 'pipe_tee', 'pipe_tee', ...]

HandleExpr (inline anonymous handlers) still uses
handler_stack_tag(handled_names) — correct, because inline
handlers have no authored name; the handled effects ARE
the identity.

two-top/0f6634b:
With PRIVATE selected, the dial now shows its own join QR (the share
module's renderer, on builds with TWOTOP_WATCH_URL baked): the link is
the Pages host's join.html carrying #<CODE>-<arena>. The other phone's
system camera opens that page — the code huge, the table named — and
its OPEN IN 2-TOP button is a twotop://join/<CODE>-<arena> deep link.
Stock camera apps won't launch custom schemes but browsers will, so
the page is the bridge: scan with the camera, tap once in the browser,
land in the app. A phone without the app gets the APK link and dials
by hand; either way both phones tap DUEL AT the same code as ever.

App-side, the manifest gains the twotop scheme intent filter
(cargo-apk metadata; custom scheme on purpose — https app-links need
domain verification at the domain root, which the Pages subpath cannot
host) and a PostStartup JNI read of getIntent().getDataString()
parses the launch URI into the dial slots and the arena pick, after
the persisted restores so the link's pick wins the boot it arrived
on. parse_join refuses anything that is not exactly a code and a
known table — a QR is typed by nobody, so there is no fuzziness to
forgive. The android half compiles under the APK workflow's NDK env
(bare cargo check lacks it locally); the two-phone scan is the
operator gate.
tokensafe/0f4793b:
5 independent optimizations to reduce degraded results and extend
effective daily capacity from ~6,600 to ~11,000 checks at zero cost:

1. Adaptive token age: 2-phase getSignaturesForAddress (limit:2 probe
   → limit:100 if needed). Saves ~900 RPC credits/check.
2. Degraded result caching: 30s TTL instead of skip. Prevents RPC
   hammering on transient failures.
3. withRetry helper: single retry with 500ms delay for transient errors
   (timeout/429/503/ECONNRESET). Applied to token-age, top-holders,
   metadata.
4. CLMM LP lock skip: Raydium CLMM pools skip LP lock detection
   (positions, not fungible LP tokens). Saves 1-2 RPC calls.
5. Conditional PDA Phase 2: program resolution only when concentration
   high enough to affect scoring (top10>30% or top1>10%).
